note: One row per reference FLOW state of each adopted app (R-241): the harvested states plus the states found by driving the adopted app. Every state has a disposition — bound (a live verifier assertion proves it over daemon truth), refused (the app refuses it by name; a test proves the refusal), named_gap (visible on the surface as `shown_as`), or open (known and not yet handled — the census counts these down to zero). A proof names a file and the EXACT text of an assertion or test in it, so renaming one breaks the link. No tenant data: labels are the reference's own UI words.

Creating a type is not bound over ODK: the reference saves a type only with a backing datasource and an object data store (its review lists "Backing datasource is missing"), and an ODK type has one only when materialized (odk-materialized-object-sets)

states.label: Editing a type (every type and link page)
states.reason: the pages say "You do not have edit permissions", which is false. Driven with edit permission on (isolated stack), a description edit reaches Review changes, and Save to ontology stays disabled: "Backing datasource is missing" and no data store. An ODK type is backed only when materialized, so editing waits on binding a type's materialized set as its datasource, then saves as an ODK patch at the expected revision
